question: Does the standard grower, one seed click and 0 correction minutes on PHerc0841's regular 9.366 um scan, give a 20 x 12 mm surface that reads rows for a blind human?
window: PHerc0841 known-text window W (20 x 11.7 mm); the two grows were assembled into W's frame and read with the canonical 2.4 um reader (same chain as the control)
raters: sebastien (can only upgrade to two raters)

arm.grown: arm: the standard grower on PHerc0841's regular 9.366 um scan, one seed click per half and 0 correction minutes, two growth-sized grows assembled over the window (0.98 coverage), read with the 2.4 um reader

control.ctrl: readable control: w00's own render of the window

pictures.guard: one not-rows guard per rater (see the page facts)
pictures.calib: calibration: a known-rows ink map of another public fragment's known text (not this window), a picture both raters had rated before
pictures.calib_blank: the calibration map in the wrong layer order (wrong-order blank)

per_rater.VOID: a picture unanswered, the calibration or the w00 control not called rows, a wrong-order blank (grown_blank or calibration blank) called rows, or the guard called rows
per_rater.GROWER-READS: else the grown tile called rows

scope: both raters know W's text; one seed's half sits a median 200 um from w00 (very likely partly another winding); the frozen row score and the AI agent screen put the field far below the control (numbers file)
